Where it began

Ben Duckett was born in Farnborough on 17 October 1994 and went to school at Stowe. He was in the first year of his A-levels when Northamptonshire handed him his debut, in a Twenty20 match against Gloucestershire in July 2012, and that same year he went to the Under-19 World Cup with England.

In 2015 he passed a thousand first-class runs for the season, with four Championship hundreds. The summer after that was something else: he opened it with 282 not out against Sussex, added hundreds of 185, 189 and 205, and helped Northants win the T20 Blast. The players' association named him both its young cricketer and its player of the year, the first man to collect the pair in one season.

The player

His Test debut came in Bangladesh in 2016, where he made a fifty in his second match. The real start of his Test story, though, came six years later in Pakistan. Batting alongside Zak Crawley, he was part of the fastest England opening stand to reach a hundred and the fastest double-century partnership in all Test cricket, 233 balls.

After that he became a fixture. His best Test score, 182, came against Ireland in 2023, and at Headingley in 2025 he made 62 and 149 to steer England home in a chase of 371, which made him player of the match. By November 2026 he had played 49 Tests for England, making 3,364 runs at 38.23 with seven hundreds and 16 fifties.

What made him special

Duckett scored quickly and rarely looked troubled while he did it. That made him a natural fit for the attacking style England took up under Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum, and his partnerships with Crawley often had the scoreboard spinning before the bowlers had settled.

It did not always come off, which is the price an opener pays for trying to take the game away from the bowlers in the first hour. When it did, the match tended to look very different by lunch.

Away from the middle

He moved from Northamptonshire to Nottinghamshire in 2018 and became a mainstay there, with 1,012 runs in the 2022 Championship as the county won Division Two. He captained Welsh Fire in The Hundred and played for Birmingham Phoenix, and in December 2025 Delhi Capitals picked him in the auction for the 2026 IPL.

In one-day cricket he made 165 against Australia at the 2025 Champions Trophy, for a while the highest score anyone had made in that tournament. He was also named one of Wisden's Cricketers of the Year.

And finally

In 2019 he made a double hundred for Nottinghamshire from 168 balls against Cambridge students, the fastest by a Notts batter in first-class cricket. The university bowlers may have heard he liked to get on with things. Nobody can have told them quite how much.
